How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide that shows you how to **generate a RESTful API request** for the *“Get information of device connector versions”* endpoint in **Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1**. I’ll cover: | What | How | |------|-----| | **1. Find the endpoint** | Use the built‑in API Explorer or the API docs. | | **2. Prepare authentication** | Get a bearer token (or use basic auth if your instance is configured that way). | | **3. Build the request** | Set the URL, HTTP method, headers, and optional query parameters. | | **4. Test & copy the request** | Run it in the Explorer, then copy the generated code snippet. | | **5. Execute programmatically** | Example `curl` and Python `requests` snippets. | | **6. (Optional) Use the helper function** | If you have the exact URL, you can call the `requests_get` function. | --- ## 1. Locate the Endpoint 1. **Log in** to your Cisco Nexus Dashboard UI. 2. In the left‑hand navigation pane, click **“API Explorer”** (or **“Developer Tools → API Explorer”**). 3. In the search box, type **“device connector versions”** or the exact API name you mentioned. 4. The Explorer will list the matching endpoint, e.g.: ``` GET /api/v1/device-connector-versions ``` > **Tip:** If you’re not seeing the endpoint, double‑check that you’re on the correct API version (6.3.1) and that your user role has API access. --- ## 2. Prepare Authentication The Nexus Dashboard uses **OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens** for API calls. If you don’t already have a token: 1. In the UI, go to **“User Settings → API Tokens”**. 2. Click **“Generate Token”** and copy the token. 3. Store it securely; you’ll need it in the `Authorization` header. > **Alternative** – If your instance is configured for basic auth, you can use `Authorization: Basic `. --- ## 3. Build the Request | Element | Example | Notes | |---------|---------|-------| | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | The API is read‑only. | | **URL** | `https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions` | Replace `` with your actual host (e.g., `nexus-dashboard.company.com`). | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | Add any other headers required by your environment. | | **Query Parameters** | None for this endpoint (unless you want to filter). | If the API supports filters, add them as `?param=value`. | **Full example (plain text):** ``` GET https://nexus-dashboard.company.com/api/v1/device-connector-versions Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9... Accept: application/json ``` --- ## 4. Test & Copy the Request 1. In the **API Explorer**, paste the URL into the “Endpoint” field. 2. Click **“Send Request”**. 3. The Explorer will display the response body (JSON) and the raw request/response headers. 4. Click **“Copy Code”** → choose your preferred language (e.g., `curl`, `Python`, `JavaScript`). 5. Paste the snippet into your editor or terminal. --- ## 5. Execute Programmatically ### a. `curl` ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://nexus-dashboard.company.com/api/v1/device-connector-versions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN_HERE" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` ### b. Python (`requests`) ```python import requests url = "https://nexus-dashboard.company.com/api/v1/device-connector-versions" headers = { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN_HERE", "Accept": "application/json", } response = requests.get(url, headers=headers) response.raise_for_status() # Raises an error for 4xx/5xx responses data = response.json() print(data) ``` > **Note:** Replace `YOUR_TOKEN_HERE` with the token you generated earlier. --- ## 6. (Optional) Use the Helper Function If you have the exact URL and want to fetch the JSON directly from within a Python environment that has the `requests_get` helper, you can do: ```python from functions import requests_get result = requests_get({ "url": "https://nexus-dashboard.company.com/api/v1/device-connector-versions", "params": {} # Add query params here if needed }) print(result) ``` > **Important:** The helper assumes you’ve already set up authentication globally (e.g., via environment variables or a session). If not, you’ll need to pass the `Authorization` header manually. --- ## Quick Checklist - [ ] Logged into Nexus Dashboard UI. - [ ] Found the correct endpoint in API Explorer. - [ ] Generated a bearer token (or have basic auth credentials). - [ ] Built the request with proper URL, headers, and method. - [ ] Tested in Explorer and copied the code snippet. - [ ] Ran the request locally (curl/Python). Once you have the JSON response, you can parse it to extract the device connector version information you need. If you run into any errors (e.g., 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found), double‑check the token, host, and endpoint path. Happy querying!
